mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national authority in country of origin (e.g., police department or passport office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent Ministry of Foreign Affairs or designated authority of the issuing state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement) for each founder, director, or beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed bank in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy with Hague Apostille where the issuer is a public entity, or certified translation into French for private document types

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National court registry, public prosecutor's office, or designated judicial records authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus certified French translation by a sworn/appointed translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and good standing of any foreign corporate shareholder (if applicable)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registry of the foreign shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus certified French translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP screening of all founding shareholders, managers, and beneficial owners under Article L.561-10 of the Code monétaire et financier; mandatory sanctions screening against UN/EU consolidated sanctions lists, OFAC (SDN and Sectoral Sanctions Identifications), French national terrorism list, and Tracfin adverse media alerts. KYC files must be retained for at least five years after the commercial relationship ends, and risk-based ongoing monitoring applies.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises de l'INPI — formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, interfaced with the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) and Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name of a Société par Actions Simplifiée must be written in Latin characters, allow accents and standard punctuation, and any foreign-language words must be transliterated and/or accompanied by a French or Latin-script form. All constitutional documents, including the articles of association, must be drafted in French; bilingual versions are permitted only as unofficial convenience translations.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate a standalone name-reservation certificate; the proposed name is checked and reserved automatically upon acceptance of the incorporation filing through the INPI Guichet unique. If the registry rejects the proposed name, the applicant may: (i) resubmit a corrected name through the same Guichet unique portal; (ii) file an administrative appeal or référé devant le Président du Tribunal de commerce within 30 days of the rejection decision where the rejection is for grounds covered by Articles L.123-1 et seq. of the Code de commerce; or (iii) if the refusal cites a prior trademark or company-name conflict, initiate opposition or invalidation proceedings before the intellectual property judge at the Tribunal judiciaire de Paris. The rejection notice must state the legal basis, de-identified conflicting record, and applicable appeal deadline.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable with statutory restrictions: a French SAS may establish its registered office with an authorized domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) for a maximum aggregate period of five years. After that period, a physical headquarters address in France is mandatory. Virtual offices are generally permissible for this low-risk e-commerce industry but must receive mail and be capable of presenting corporate records during tax or registry audits.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low quantified risk, estimated at 5–10% annual probability. Unannounced physical inspections are unlikely for standard garden-technology e-commerce registrations, but a flag from anti-fraud algorithms (e.g., abnormally high VAT recovery or inconsistent EU cross-border sales) can trigger an on-site inspection by the tax administration or fraud specialists.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce (French Commercial Code), Book II, Title II, Chapter VII, Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 (Société par Actions Simplifiée); general incorporation provisions of Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10; RCS registration rules of Articles L.123-1 to L.123-12; Decree No. 2019-1061 and the INPI Guichet unique implementing decree of 9 June 2022; PACTE Act No. 2019-486 abolishing the minimum capital threshold.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) kept by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered office, operating through the INPI single electronic portal (Guichet unique — formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); INSEE attributes the SIREN and SIRET identifiers upon registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts de constitution signed by all shareholders, filed together with the standard M0 declaration of incorporation, submitted electronically to the Guichet unique and inscribed in the RCS; the official company extract issued is the extrait Kbis.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital applies to an SAS; the amount set in the Statuts must be fully subscribed. Cash contributions must be deposited into an escrow account (licensed bank, notaire, or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations) before filing and may be released only after the RCS registration of the company; in-kind contributions require a valuation report of a commissaire aux apports unless waived unanimously by the shareholders.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE SOCIÉTÉ PAR ACTIONS SIMPLIFIÉE [COMPANY NAME] — The shareholders, having subscribed in full to the share capital, hereby: RESOLVE, first, to confirm the subscription of [NUMBER] ordinary shares composing the share capital of [AMOUNT] euros, fully paid in cash/in-kind. RESOLVE, second, to establish the registered office at [ADDRESS], within the territorial jurisdiction of the RCS, and to approve the lease and occupancy agreement. RESOLVE, third, to appoint [NAME] as President, and [NAME] as Statutory Auditor, with powers set out in the Statuts. RESOLVE, finally, to ratify all pre-incorporation acts and to authorize the President to complete all registrations before the competent registry authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and Distinctiveness Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) and INPI corporate data repository (data.inpi.fr)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a formal search for identical or confusingly similar corporate names in the RCS and for conflicting trademarks in the INPI national register. Validate the proposed SAS name and obtain a search report. The name must be lawful and distinctive and must not be reserved by another legal entity; an optional national trademark application may be filed simultaneously with INPI for exclusive protection.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is queried for identity with an existing registration, file a voluntary substitution of the name before filing or negotiate a coexistence agreement with the conflicting rights holder; any change to the name must be reflected in the Statuts and re-signed by all shareholders.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), under the Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté industrielle et numérique; online services accessible via https://www.impots.gouv.fr. Business registration and VAT number procurement coordinated through the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via Infogreffe and the CFE/Guichet unique managed by the INPI.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS, including one wholly owned by non-residents, obtains its tax identity by filing the standard incorporation dossier (M0 plus supporting documents, e.g., statutory auditors, shareholding identification, principal shareholder statements) through the electronic one-stop shop (Guichet unique) administered by INPI. The DGFiP automatically assigns the SIREN (national company number) and SIRET (establishment number), and the VAT number (numéro de TVA intracommunautaire FRXXXX) is issued once the company is registered at RCS. Non-established foreign entities making taxable supplies in France without an EU establishment must request direct VAT registration from the DGFiP's Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) and, in certain circumstances, appoint a fiscal representative established in France who is jointly and severally liable for VAT. For intra-EU e-commerce distance sales and imports, the non-resident may instead use the Union One-Stop Shop (OSS) or Import One-Stop Shop (IOSS) regimes rather than full French VAT registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A SAS is a capital company (société de capitaux) and is unconditionally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) on its worldwide profits, subject to the regime of territoriality (régime territorial) which exempts profits of permanently-established foreign branches and does not allow deduction of related foreign losses. There is no pass-through or fiscal transparency treatment available for a SAS under French domestic law; the EU Anti-Tax-Avoidance-Directive and hybrid mismatch rules do not alter this default. Tax_Exempt_Zone is not applicable to the standard commercial profit center; however, specific territorial tax reliefs (e.g., zones franches d'activités, régime fiscal de Corse, or IFER exemptions) are available only as narrowly-scoped incentives and do not change the overall entity-level IS status.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France operates no general check-the-box election akin to the U.S. 'eligible entity' classification. The principal elections relevant to a French SAS are: (1) election under CGI Article 223 A to form an intégration fiscale (tax group) with French subsidiaries if the SAS holds at least 95% of the shares directly or indirectly; (2) election for the 'régime fiscal des sociétés mères' (mother-daughter regime) allowing 95% exemption of dividend income, coupled with the optional EBIT/dividend quota mechanism; (3) election under Article 239 quater C for a SARL to be treated as transparent, not available for a SAS; (4) annual option, if eligible, for the VAT réel simplifié regime; and (5) application of the French hybrid mismatch neutralization rules under CGI Article 212 bis and the ATAD 1 rules (interest limitation, CFC, exit taxation), which are mandatory rather than elective. There is no check-the-box election to treat a French SAS as a partnership for French tax or for U.S. check-the-box mapping; U.S. or other foreign owners may inadvertently create a CFC or PFIC from the foreign side but the SAS remains an entity-level taxpayer in France.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA – Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée), governed by CGI Articles 256 to 290 quater and the French Tax Code implementing Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a French-established SAS: mandatory VAT registration from the first taxable transaction (no statutory de minimis threshold). For intra-EU cross-border distance sales of goods to non-taxable persons (e-commerce), the European-wide annual distance-sales threshold applicable via the One-Stop Shop (OSS) is €10,000; below that threshold, a French vendor may apply French VAT throughout the EU, and once the €10,000 aggregate threshold is exceeded, the vendor must account for VAT in each destination Member State via the OSS. There is no separate French domestic turnover threshold for online sales of gardening equipment by an already-established SAS; the company is already registered. A foreign e-commerce seller without a French establishment becomes subject to French VAT from its first sale into France unless it uses the IOSS for consignment stocks or low-value imports, in which case the IOSS threshold per consignment is €150.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is phasing in a mandatory B2B electronic invoicing and e-reporting reform. Beginning 1 September 2024, all businesses must be able to receive structured electronic invoices via the Chorus Pro platform or through accredited Private Digital Platforms (PDPs); from 1 September 2026, all B2B e-invoicing becomes compulsory, and B2C transaction data (e-reporting) must be transmitted in near-real-time to the DGFiP. In the interim, electronic cash-register software used for B2C sales must be certified or self-declared as compliant with Articles 286-2 and 290 CGI and the NF 525 / NF 550 technical certification. There is no current general real-time fiscal stamping/clearance mechanism for ordinary e-commerce like the Italian 'lotteria degli scontrini' or a continuous controls system; however, the DGFiP requires the periodic transmission of VAT return data via the professional portal, and exports are separately monitored through the customs export declaration system (DELTA/GUN). Invoices issued to French public-sector entities must be transmitted through Chorus Pro under Decree No. 92-466. The e-invoice must use a compliant format (Factur-X, UBL, CII) and contain mandatory French VAT fields, including the intra-Community VAT numbers of both parties, when supplies are intra-EU.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A French SAS may apply the 0% VAT rate (exonération à l'exportation) under CGI Article 262-I-1 for goods physically removed from France to a destination outside the European Union, provided the sale is evidenced by the transport of goods out of the EU territory. The exporter must hold documentary proof of export (preuve d'exportation) in the form prescribed by Revenue (BOI-TVA-CHAMP-30-10-10), normally an electronic or paper Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'Échanges de Marchandises) via DELTA, corroborated by a transport document (CMR, bill of lading, airway bill, or postal receipt) and, for certain transport modalities, the customs exit confirmation. Intra-EU dispatches to a VAT-registered customer are not 'export zero-rating' but rather exempt non-collection under Article 262 ter CGI, qualifying on the basis of the customer's valid EU VAT number, Intrastat or recapitulative statement reporting, and proof of physical movement into the other Member State within the statutory deadlines (generally not later than the 15th day of the month following the quarter). Services directly connected to exported goods (FOB/transport services) may also be zero-rated under Article 259 D CGI when the recipient's effective establishment is outside the EU; digital/e-commerce services to consumers are subject to OSS rather than export zero-rating. Because the underlying platform sale of hydroponics equipment is treated as a distance sale of goods, the zero-rating applies only to the physical export movements, not to the mere sale of hardware or software downloads unless outside the EU.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'Échanges de Marchandises / DAE) submitted via the DELTA customs system and bearing the enforceable exit date
Export commercial invoice (facture commerciale d'exportation) with complete seller and buyer identification, breakdown of VAT treatment, and Incoterms clause
Transport evidence: Bill of Lading (B/L) or International Consignment Note (CMR) or Air Waybill or Post Office receipt for postal exports, showing the destination outside the EU

Proof of exit from EU customs territory (exit confirmation from the customs office of export or, for non-EU transit, the final customs office) and any dual-use or agricultural documentation if applicable

Bank documentation supporting receipt of payment from the foreign buyer, such as the SWIFT MT103/MT202 receipt or an Inward Remittance Certificate if the foreign exchange/immigration regime so requires

Where an intra-EU dispatch is involved instead of an export outside the EU: valid EU VAT number of the customer as separately verified through the VIES electronic database, the recapitulative statement (état récapitulatif / EC Sales List), and dispatch proof
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGFiP applies increased audit scrutiny to export zero-rating claims, requiring full documentary proof of physical exit. If the documentary bundle is incomplete, false, or fabricated, the initial zero-rating is reversed and the full 20% French VAT is assessed on the ex-VAT sale price, triggering: late payment interest (intérêt de retard at 0.20% per month, i.e., 2.4% annually), plus an automatic 5% penalty (majoration) solely for late tax filing, and a 40% systematic penalty (insuffisance de déclaration) under CGI Article 1731; in cases of bad faith or dissimulation of facts, the penalty rises to 80% (Article 1729); if the fraudulent substance is established, criminal prosecution under Article 1741 CGI may lead to fines up to €500,000 (increased to €1,000,000 in aggravated cases), imprisonment up to five years, and posting/banishing sanctions. The clawback period for assessed VAT is generally the current calendar year plus three prior calendar years (six years in certain cases of non-filed or late-filed returns, or derived from undisclosed beneficial-owner facts), and Belgium and France trigger joint liability for falsified intra-EU claims where a self-supply has not been accounted for; the fraudster and any accomplices are solidarily liable under Article 1741. Furthermore, an entity relying on a deliberately false Inward Remittance Certificate or on a nominal 'commissionnaire' arrangement to simulate exports is exposed to tax fraud prosecution and an even higher 100% penalty in cases of deliberate non-invoicing or pure withholding on groundless exports; the French customs administration may also institute import- and export-control offenses. To mitigate audit risk, the SAS should retain a full export file (DAE, transport contract, insurance certificate, delivery notes) for at least six years after the tax period and reconcile export data quarterly with the EC Sales List and Intrastat filings. A failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days also triggers French foreign-exchange regulation sanctions, includes the application of the Malta or similar indexation rules when applicable, and can be used by the tax authority as evidence of simulating an export transaction in order to deny both the zero-rating and the corresponding exemption from VAT on services.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), together with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) for international capital movement oversight and balance-of-payments reporting; ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) supervises banking and payment-institution conduct.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France maintains full current and capital account convertibility under Articles 63-66 TFEU and the French Monetary and Financial Code. No general exchange-control authorization is required for a French SAS to receive foreign equity contributions, repatriate funds, or convert EUR to foreign currency. Profit remittance hurdles are primarily tax-related: dividends paid by a French SAS to non-resident shareholders are subject to French withholding tax at the statutory 25% rate unless reduced under an applicable double-tax treaty, and the distribution must be approved by the shareholders in accordance with SAS corporate formalities. Additional operational constraints include EU financial sanctions screening, FATCA/CRS reporting, and Banque de France balance-of-payments statistical filings; these are not currency-convertibility restrictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirements and no mandatory conversion ratios in France or the Eurozone. Export receipts may be retained in EUR or foreign currency in accounts held with authorized credit institutions. Banks require underlying commercial documentation for credit of export proceeds, and Banque de France may require balance-of-payments reporting for transactions above regulatory thresholds. All payments remain subject to AML/KYC controls and EU/OFAC-style sanctions screening.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital injection escrow/blocked account and operational multi-currency EUR account
Operational EUR current account with international settlement and FX desk
Operational account and trade-finance account for supplier settlements
Operational account for cash pooling and wholesale FX hedging

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium as a supplementary payment channel but Low as the sole banking solution. EU/EEA-licensed electronic money institutions passporting into France may provide IBAN accounts, local collecting, and SEPA/CBPR+ payment rails, but they are not credit institutions and are generally unsuitable for capital escrow, FX hedging, overdrafts, or documentary trade finance. Offshore digital EMIs without an EU/EEA license may not lawfully hold client funds or provide payment services to a French entity; using such providers creates regulatory, tax, and treasury-control risks. Any fintech/EMI solution must verify ACPR authorization or valid EU passport notification, maintain independent client accounts, and execute full French-standard KYC/UBO identity verification.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French AML law allows remote onboarding using regulated video identification and qualified electronic signatures, but French Tier-1 banks commonly require physical attendance of the SAS legal representative, at least one director, and the ultimate beneficial owner for corporate account opening. A remote opening is possible only if the bank accepts eIDAS-qualified digital identity verification and the KYC file is complete, including certified corporate documents. For this non-resident-owned French SAS structure, the prudent blueprint is to schedule in-person director/UBO appearances at the selected bank's French branch; remote-only onboarding should be treated as exception, not assumption.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EU ultimate beneficial owner behind a French SAS without recognizable local economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current French Kbis extract, articles of association, beneficial-owner declaration filed with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, full UBO corporate-chain chart, certified passports of directors and UBOs, French business-address proof, and a commercial business plan for the online retail hydroponics equipment operation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Injection of initial capital by a foreign shareholder raises source-of-funds and third-party-payment questions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholders' resolution authorizing capital contribution, bank statement of the contributing corporate shareholder, SWIFT MT103 confirming the sending account and reference, notarized declaration of source of funds, audited or official financial statements of the subscriber, and an unencumbered-funds certification from the remitting bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce model relying on Stripe/PayPal payment aggregators is flagged for high-volume cross-border activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed Stripe/PayPal merchant agreements, transaction and payout records, website and supply-chain contracts, refund and chargeback policies, VAT registration certificate if applicable, and evidence that customer funds flow through regulated PSP accounts into the French SAS's corporate bank account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-residency mismatch or reliance on France-China treaty benefits for future profit distributions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificates of tax residence for each non-resident shareholder, legal ownership structure, substance documentation, dividend distribution policy, and transfer-pricing documentation for any cross-border intra-group service or goods transactions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SWIFT MT103 (or ISO 20022 pain.001) from the shareholder's corporate bank account directly to the French SAS's dedicated capital contribution account with a BIC/IBAN of the French receiving bank. The payment must include clear remittance information identifying the purpose as 'augmentation de capital / apport en capital' and reference the shareholder resolution and notarial/corporate filing. No third-party payers are acceptable. For remittances from China, the sending bank will require underlying corporate documentation such as the French company registration certificate, share subscription agreement, and a declaration of cross-border equity investment for SAFE filing. The French receiving bank must verify the UBO structure and record the transaction for Banque de France balance-of-payments reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For supplier and trade settlements, the acceptable clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 for direct bank-to-bank payment to the beneficiary, SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) through TARGET2 for EUR payments within the EEA, and commercial documentary letters of credit issued under UCP 600 via SWIFT MT700/MT710 for secured import transactions. Disbursements must be supported by commercial invoices, purchase orders, bills of lading or packing lists, and where applicable customs declarations. All outbound transfers must be screened against sanctions lists and money-laundering indicators, and the French bank may require the underlying trade documentation before releasing funds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forward contracts (change à terme) executed with an ACPR-authorized credit institution for EUR/CNY or EUR/USD hedging
FX swaps (swap de change) covering matched inbound and outbound cash-flow dates
Cross-currency swaps for converting long-term shareholder loans or capital exposures
FX vanilla options with documented underlying commercial exposure
Non-deliverable forwards permissible only where a specific third-currency exposure cannot be settled onshore and the hedge is fully evidenced by trade documents
